subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who targets the Ettin during the ambush, and recognizes the behavior of Derro avoiding Narrak as similar to Priestesses of Lolth silencing their subordinates.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak. I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts darkness to conceal the Derro, breathes fire into it, warns of a madness-inducing effect from the ritual circle, and later moves the darkness over Narrak to break the fear spell.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful! I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is struck by a Derro, vomits acid after incantation, casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, and is affected by Narrak’s fear spell before being freed by Zalthir’s darkness.
source_quote: One of the Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness, notices Grygum, and strikes him while chanting, “You shall die! You shall die!” ... I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist who leads the ritual chant, berates the Derro for lack of vigor, casts fear using a white feather, and is trapped in Zalthir’s darkness after being targeted by Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified. ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is targeted by Narrak’s fear spell, is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while frightened, and attempts to strike the Ettin with success after the fear is broken.
source_quote: The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered. ... But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a Derro possessed by a ghost who is tied up after concern he might lose control, and later speaks about death as a form of sleep while being untied.
source_quote: I haven’t had a good night's sleep in ages. Although it’s unclear if I am sleeping … There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: cultist cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of the ritual, where Derro chant around a platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, and where the Ember Vanguard sneaks in undetected.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern. And once again, we have managed to sneak into the room.

subject: platform
fact: The platform holds a statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it, and is surrounded by Derro during the ritual.
source_quote: There is a statue of another two-headed stone giant. ... They all move to their positions. ... A statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it.

subject: statue of stone giant
fact: The statue is a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, located on the platform, and is mistaken by Zalthir as being massive until he realizes its true size.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: white feather
fact: The white feather is used by Narrak to cast a fear spell on Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: book in chief cultist's hands
fact: The book in the chief cultist's hands contains the ritual chant used by the Derro, and is referenced as the source of the incantation.
source_quote: Ah, the book in the chief cultist's hands.

subject: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp is cast by Daz to trap Narrak in the darkness, causing him to scream in rage.
source_quote: And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is. ... Narrak screams in rage - “You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!”

subject: scorching rays
fact: Daz casts three spears of flame as scorching rays, roaring with orange and red hues, aimed at the Ettin.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed creature targeted by Daz, struck by Thorin and Grygum, and attacks the frightened Thorin with its morning star.
source_quote: I say the Ettin. ... The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. ... A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are the chanting cultists who perform the ritual, are concealed by Zalthir’s darkness, attack Grygum and Zalthir, and are berated by Narrak for lack of vigor.
source_quote: Five Derro are chanting. ... One of the Derro raises a hand, and asks where, and the head cultist shouts, “OVER THERE!!!” ... Another Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness and attacks Grygum, missing.

subject: death dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, and one Derro is preoccupied with trying not to be noticed by it.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: ritual chant performed by Derro
fact: The Derro chant a ritual invoking Demogorgon, with lines about madness, city drooling, spirals turning, and grafting more heads, as part of a failed ritual interrupted by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: Hear me, you two-headed fools! His madness flows, our city drools! From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn! For Demogorgon, the city will burn! More heads for grafting! More for the pile!

subject: fear spell cast by Narrak
fact: Narrak casts a fear spell using a white feather, affecting Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, until Zalthir moves the darkness over him, breaking the effect.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified. ... I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: acid vomit from Grygum
fact: Grygum vomits a wave of acid after an incantation, a side effect of his magic that is not a spell he wishes to cast.
source_quote: I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. This is not a spell I wish to cast.

subject: Zalthir’s darkness concealment
fact: Zalthir casts darkness over the Derro, concealing them from view and enabling the Ember Vanguard to launch a surprise attack.
source_quote: He plans to use his darkness, and wants to know who I will target. I say the Ettin. He nods and soon all the derro are covered in his magical darkness.

subject: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on Narrak
fact: Daz casts Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on Narrak while he is hidden in darkness, trapping him and causing him to scream about an inevitable curse.
source_quote: And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is. ... Narrak screams in rage - “You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!”

subject: Derro’s failed ritual
fact: The Derro’s ritual fails due to lack of vigor, mispronunciation, and interruption by the Ember Vanguard, despite Narrak’s repeated commands for more passion.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly, at which point the one I assume is Narrak, like every choir director ever shouts, “Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it!"

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the previous stronghold of the cult, from which the Ember Vanguard departs before returning to the cultist cavern.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar bets Grygum that his knots on Pelek will not hold, and later loses the bet when Pelek remains tied up the next day.
source_quote: JimJar again offers one of his silly bets. He bets me that my knots won’t hold. ... And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid speaks to Zalthir about Rump-a-dump, insists on non-violence toward her kind, and claims they convert enemies into zombies, before falling asleep after Zalthir’s frustration.
source_quote: The childlike voice of the Myconid. ... “Rump-a-dump would never let them do that! You don’t want to help my friends, and so why should I help you?” ... And the creature falls asleep.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the one who notices the need to stop the ritual, but his spells are almost finished, and he later receives divine insight that Hgraam can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants.
source_quote: Grygum turns to me, “I know we want to stop this ritual, but my spells are almost finished.” ... We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is referenced as a divine entity who can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants, invoked by Grygum’s divine insight.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is the demon invoked in the ritual chant, described as the Prince of Chaos whose madness flows through the cultists.
source_quote: For Demogorgon, the city will burn! ... Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the city targeted by the cult’s ritual, which they intend to lay waste to after converting more Stone Giants.
source_quote: Now we shall convert one more, and by golly, they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Whorlstone
fact: Whorlstone is the location from whose depths the spirals turn, referenced in the ritual chant as the origin of the magic.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the choir-like head cultist who directs the Derro’s ritual, uses fear magic, and is ultimately trapped by Daz’s spell.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Derro’s chant variation
fact: The Derro perform a second chant during the ritual, with altered lines about the Deepking falling and Narrak’s vision, after being corrected by Narrak.
source_quote: Two heads! Two heads! A glorious sight! The Deepking falls into endless night! Narrak's vision, sharp and keen! The Prince of Chaos, always unseen!

subject: Zalthir’s meditation interrupted
fact: Zalthir attempts to meditate but is interrupted by the Myconid, who insists on talking about Rump-a-dump and the nature of myconid-zombie conversion.
source_quote: I look forward to meditating when my thoughts are interrupted. ... “Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair. Why don’t you listen to me!”

subject: Pelek’s binding
fact: Pelek is bound by the group after concern he might lose control of the Derro body, and remains tied up overnight.
source_quote: Daz, however, explains that there is no such danger. And that they would all be safer with the ghost tied up. ... And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up.

subject: Daz’s scorching rays strike
fact: Daz hurls three spears of scorching flame at the Ettin, feeling empowered and invigorated as the flames roar like beasts.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath in darkness
fact: Zalthir breathes fire into his magical darkness, targeting the concealed Derro, but is disappointed with the outcome.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Derro’s missed attacks
fact: Two Derro attack Grygum and Zalthir in the darkness but miss their targets, indicating poor combat coordination.
source_quote: One of the Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness, notices Grygum, and strikes him while chanting, “You shall die! You shall die!” ... Another creature attacks Zalthir in the darkness. It took shrieks something intelligible. I don’t hear the sound of weapons making contact with flesh...

subject: Narrak’s emergence from darkness
fact: Narrak emerges from Zalthir’s darkness and casts fear, then is re-trapped by Daz’s Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp.
source_quote: And then Narrak emerges and shouts, “I will use fear!” ... And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is. ... Narrak screams in rage...

subject: Grygum’s guiding bolt
fact: Grygum casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, which groans and smiles, suggesting it is not as effective as intended.
source_quote: A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles. I don’t think the spell hurt him as badly as we need.

subject: Thorin’s successful strike
fact: Thorin strikes the Ettin with success after the fear spell is broken, contributing to the creature’s defeat.
source_quote: But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Myconid’s sleep
fact: The Myconid falls asleep after Zalthir’s frustration and reference to parental advice, ending her persistent interruptions.
source_quote: And the creature falls asleep.

subject: Pelek’s sleep debate
fact: Pelek reflects on whether death is a form of sleep while being untied, introducing philosophical uncertainty.
source_quote: There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: Derro’s preoccupation with death dog
fact: One Derro is so preoccupied with avoiding a death dog that he fails to notice the Ember Vanguard’s infiltration.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Narrak’s running commentary
fact: Narrak provides continuous running commentary during the battle, even as the ritual collapses, declaring the power of Demogorgon and mocking the attacks.
source_quote: Fire is nothing compared to the awesome power of Demogorgon! ... What’s going on here! ... More vigor! This city's doom needs a ritual. Dig it!

subject: Zalthir’s realization of statue size
fact: Zalthir initially believes the statue of the stone giant is massive, but is corrected when shown it is only two feet tall.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: Daz’s recognition of Lolth’s Priestesses
fact: Daz recognizes the Derro’s behavior of hiding from Narrak as identical to how subordinates hide from Priestesses of Lolth.
source_quote: I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible. A high-level cleric can kill you very easily.

subject: Zalthir’s monk training against madness
fact: Zalthir’s monk training allows him to resist the madness induced by the ritual circle’s effect.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful!

subject: Grygum’s acid vomit as magical side effect
fact: Grygum’s acid vomit is not a spell he casts, but an involuntary side effect of his incantation, which he finds repulsive.
source_quote: I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. This is not a spell I wish to cast.

subject: JimJar’s bet loss
fact: JimJar bets Grygum his knots won’t hold on Pelek, but loses when Pelek remains bound overnight.
source_quote: JimJar again offers one of his silly bets. He bets me that my knots won’t hold. ... And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: Myconid’s zombie conversion claim
fact: The Myconid claims they convert dead enemies into zombies, and insists Rump-a-dump would never allow such a fate for allies.
source_quote: We have this process that allows us to convert our dead enemies into zombies. ... Rump-a-dump would never let them do that!

subject: Narrak’s ritual failure
fact: Narrak’s ritual fails due to Derro incompetence, magical interference, and physical attack, despite his repeated commands for vigor.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly... ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Zalthir’s darkness used tactically
fact: Zalthir uses darkness not only for concealment but as a tactical tool to disrupt Narrak’s fear spell by moving it over the caster.
source_quote: I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Daz’s scorching rays as expression of inner fury
fact: Daz describes his scorching rays as vessels of his inner fury, roaring like beasts, indicating emotional investment in his magic.
source_quote: These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Pelek’s existential uncertainty
fact: Pelek expresses uncertainty about whether he is sleeping or dead, blurring the line between life, death, and possession.
source_quote: Although it’s unclear if I am sleeping … There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: Derro’s failed coordination
fact: The Derro repeatedly fail to coordinate their chant and attacks, leading to missed strikes and ritual failure.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly... ... Another Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness and attacks Grygum, missing.

subject: Zalthir’s meditation interrupted by Myconid
fact: Zalthir’s attempt at meditation is persistently interrupted by the Myconid’s emotional demands about Rump-a-dump and non-violence.
source_quote: I look forward to meditating when my thoughts are interrupted. ... “Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair. Why don’t you listen to me!”

subject: Grygum’s divine insight
fact: Grygum receives divine insight that Hgraam can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants, guiding his decision-making.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Narrak’s fear spell cast
fact: Narrak casts fear using a white feather, affecting three members of the Ember Vanguard until the source is obscured.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: Ettin’s survival despite damage
fact: The Ettin survives multiple attacks, including a guiding bolt and Thorin’s strike, and smiles after being hit, suggesting resilience or corruption.
source_quote: A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles. ... But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath disappointment
fact: Zalthir is disappointed with the outcome of his fire breath in the darkness, suggesting it was ineffective against the Derro.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Daz’s targeting of Ettin
fact: Daz selects the Ettin as his primary target during the ambush, indicating strategic priority.
source_quote: He plans to use his darkness, and wants to know who I will target. I say the Ettin.

subject: Narrak’s curse declaration
fact: Narrak declares that the curse spreads despite being trapped, implying the ritual’s effects are irreversible.
source_quote: You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Myconid’s emotional manipulation
fact: The Myconid uses emotional appeals and guilt to pressure Zalthir into helping Rump-a-dump, claiming he doesn’t listen to her.
source_quote: You don’t want to help my friends, and so why should I help you? ... Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair.

subject: Pelek’s binding confirmed
fact: Pelek remains bound overnight, confirming the effectiveness of Grygum’s knots and the success of the group’s precaution.
source_quote: And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: Zalthir’s final realization
fact: Zalthir realizes the statue is only two feet tall after being shown it, correcting his initial assumption of its size.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: Narrak’s fear spell
fact: Narrak casts fear using a white feather, affecting Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: Ettin’s resilience
fact: The Ettin survives multiple attacks and smiles after being hit, suggesting it is corrupted or unnaturally resilient.
source_quote: A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Zalthir’s fire breath
fact: Zalthir breathes fire into his darkness, but is disappointed with the outcome.
source_quote: Zalthir rushes into his darkness and breathes fire. He seems disappointed with the outcome.

subject: Daz’s targeting
fact: Daz selects the Ettin as his primary target during the ambush.
source_quote: He plans to use his darkness, and wants to know who I will target. I say the Ettin.

subject: Narrak’s curse declaration
fact: Narrak declares the curse spreads despite being trapped, implying the ritual’s effects are irreversible.
source_quote: You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Myconid’s emotional manipulation
fact: The Myconid uses guilt and emotional appeals to pressure Zalthir into helping Rump-a-dump.
source_quote: You don’t want to help my friends, and so why should I help you? ... Zalthir, you never listen to anything I say. It’s not fair.

subject: Pelek’s binding confirmed
fact: Pelek remains bound overnight, confirming the effectiveness of Grygum’s knots.
source_quote: And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: Zalthir’s statue realization
fact: Zalthir realizes the statue is only two feet tall after being shown it.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: Narrak’s ritual chant variation
fact: The ritual chant is repeated in two forms: the original Demogorgon invocation and a later variation with new lines.
source_quote: Hear me, you two-headed fools! ... Two heads! Two heads! A glorious sight! The Deepking falls into endless night! Narrak's vision, sharp and keen!

subject: Derro’s preoccupation with death dog
fact: One Derro is distracted by a death dog, allowing the Ember Vanguard to infiltrate undetected.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Grygum’s acid vomit
fact: Grygum vomits acid after casting a spell, an unintended and repulsive side effect.
source_quote: I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. This is not a spell I wish to cast.

subject: Zalthir’s darkness manipulation
fact: Zalthir manipulates his darkness spell to counter Narrak’s fear spell by obscuring the caster’s visibility.
source_quote: I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Narrak’s running commentary during battle
fact: Narrak continues to speak in a theatrical, dramatic tone even during active combat.
source_quote: Fire is nothing compared to the awesome power of Demogorgon! ... What’s going on here! ... More vigor! This city's doom needs a ritual. Dig it!

subject: Daz’s scorching rays
fact: Daz casts three spears of scorching flame, describing them as roaring beasts and vessels of his inner fury.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Thorin’s successful strike on Ettin
fact: Thorin lands a successful strike on the Ettin after the fear spell is broken.
source_quote: But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Myconid’s sleep
fact: The Myconid falls asleep after Zalthir’s frustration and reference to parental advice.
source_quote: And the creature falls asleep.

subject: Pelek’s existential reflection
fact: Pelek reflects on whether death is a form of sleep, introducing philosophical ambiguity about his state of being.
source_quote: There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: Derro’s failed ritual
fact: The Derro’s ritual fails due to lack of vigor, poor coordination, and interruption by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly... ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Zalthir’s monk training
fact: Zalthir’s monk training allows him to resist the madness induced by the ritual circle.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful!
